DesignSystem.title: The CANDIDATOR visual language
DesignSystem.lead: Colours, shapes, cards and decorative elements in one place. Pages are assembled from these parts. Use the moon/sun button at the top to check dark mode.

logo.title: Logo
logo.text: A flame-shaped mark, the “CANDIDATOR” wordmark and a small “AI” tag. Works on dark backgrounds too.
logo.name: CANDIDATOR

colors.title: Colours
colors.text: Primary orange, dark ink and a peach background. Every colour has a dark-mode pair.
colors.contrast1: Text on orange is dark: white text there is 2.6:1, dark text 6.2:1.
colors.contrast2: Orange text on white uses a darker shade (5.6:1). In dark mode the primary orange itself is 7.3:1.
colors.contrast3: Secondary text stays above 5:1 on the peach background too.

type.title: Typography
type.text: Inter: the ʻ mark for oʻ and gʻ, Karakalpak and Cyrillic letters in one typeface. Headings at 700–800, tight.

greeting.candidate: Hi! I'm the CANDIDATOR assistant. I'll review your resume and help make it clearer for employers. Pick one of the questions below or write your own.
greeting.employer: Hi! I can help write vacancy descriptions, screen applications and prepare interview questions. Pick a question or write your own.

candidate.improve: How can I improve my resume?
candidate.skills: Which skills does a UI/UX designer need?
candidate.interview: How should I prepare for an interview?

employer.describe: Write a vacancy text for a UI/UX designer
employer.screen: How can I screen applications quickly?
employer.questions: 5 interview questions for a frontend developer
employer.salary: What could a designer earn in Tashkent?

replies.improve: You can strengthen three things: 1) state the result of each job with a number (e.g. “raised conversion by 18%”); 2) match your skills to the words in the vacancy; 3) shorten “About me” to three lines. If you like, we can start with the first section.
replies.summary: Sample: “UI/UX designer with 3 years of experience. I work from user research to prototype on mobile apps and web services, with hands-on Figma, design systems and user testing.” Adapt the text to your own experience.
replies.skills: Core UI/UX designer skills: Figma, user research, wireframes and prototypes, design systems, accessibility basics, understanding HTML/CSS. Add a small project example for each in your resume.
replies.interview: Plan: study the company's product, practise explaining your two best projects in 3 minutes, prepare an answer to “why this solution?”, and write down two questions to ask at the end.
replies.describe: Structure: 1) short intro (team and product); 2) responsibilities (4–5 points); 3) requirements, with must-haves and nice-to-haves separate; 4) conditions and salary range in soʻm; 5) how to apply. Showing a salary range increases applications.
replies.screen: First filter by must-have requirements, then review candidates with a match above 75%. Score each candidate 1–5 on the same three criteria: experience, portfolio, communication.
replies.questions: 1) What hard problem did you solve on your last project? 2) How do you choose a state management approach? 3) How do you measure and improve page speed? 4) How do you check accessibility? 5) What do you look for in code review?
replies.salary: This is a demo answer: real market data is not connected yet. To set a range, compare experience level, job type and ranges in similar vacancies. TODO: real data.
replies.fallback: Good question! In demo mode I can only answer the suggested questions in detail. Once real AI is connected, I'll answer this too.
